def move(terrain, start, duration_s, n_runs, seed):
    import numpy as np

    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    n_steps = 60
    dt = duration_s / (n_steps - 1)

    # Arrays for lat, lon, time
    points = np.empty((n_runs, n_steps, 3), dtype=float)
    points[:, 0, 0:2] = start  # lat, lon
    points[:, 0, 2] = 0

    # initial lat/lon
    lat = np.full(n_runs, start[0])
    lon = np.full(n_runs, start[1])

    # Fixed backtrack bearing west along ridge crest ~270deg (3*pi/2)
    bearing = 3 * np.pi / 2  # radians

    # We will move in steps with distances depending on slope and speed.
    # At each step, estimate slope at current positions.
    # Use tobler's hiking function with slope and cell_m to get speed.

    # To add some realism, add small noise ±10° in bearing to mimic
    # searching for identifiable terrain backward along ridge.

    for i in range(1, n_steps):
        slope = terrain.slope_deg(lat, lon)                         # deg, vector
        elev1 = terrain.elev(lat, lon)                              # current elevation
        # propose bearing slightly randomized around west ±10°
        bearing_step = bearing + (rng.uniform(-np.pi/18, np.pi/18, n_runs))  # ±10° in rad

        # move roughly one cell in horizontal direction, modulated by dt and speed later
        dist_try = terrain.cell_m * np.ones(n_runs)  # nominal 30m step
        # compute next points by stepping dist_try along bearing_step
        lat_try, lon_try = terrain.offset(lat, lon, bearing_step, dist_try)

        # clamp lat/lon inside box
        lat_try, lon_try = terrain.clamp(lat_try, lon_try)

        # elevation next step
        elev2 = terrain.elev(lat_try, lon_try)

        # vertical and horizontal distances for slope and tobler speed
        d_elev = elev2 - elev1
        d_horiz = terrain.cell_m

        # compute tobler speed (m/s)
        speed = terrain.tobler_speed_ms(d_elev, d_horiz)

        # distance actually traveled in this dt: dist = speed * dt
        dist = speed * dt

        # restrict dist not more than terrain.cell_m (1 cell) to avoid jumps
        dist = np.minimum(dist, terrain.cell_m)

        # move along original bearing_step but with new dist
        lat_new, lon_new = terrain.offset(lat, lon, bearing_step, dist)

        # clamp into box again
        lat_new, lon_new = terrain.clamp(lat_new, lon_new)

        points[:, i, 0] = lat_new
        points[:, i, 1] = lon_new
        points[:, i, 2] = i * dt

        lat = lat_new
        lon = lon_new

    ok = terrain.inside(points[:, -1, 0], points[:, -1, 1])

    return points, ok
